howIWorkPage.title: How I work
howIWorkPage.description: The principles I bring to engineering and collaboration: useful work, shared success, candor, curiosity, fairness, and responsibility.
howIWorkPage.label: Personal values
howIWorkPage.introduction: I want to build useful things with people who trust one another. I measure my contribution by the problems we solve, the quality of the result, and whether my teammates are better able to do their work. These are the standards I choose to practice.

principles.title: Serve a worthwhile purpose
principles.body: Understand who benefits from the work and why it matters. Let that purpose guide tradeoffs. Consider the people affected by a system, including those who never chose to use it.

principles.title: Make the team stronger
principles.body: Share context, credit, and useful tools. Help across boundaries when the work needs it. Take responsibility for my contribution without presenting a shared achievement as a solo performance. Success should not require someone else on the team to lose.

principles.title: Pair high standards with respect
principles.body: Prepare thoroughly, deliver carefully, and welcome rigorous review. Treat colleagues, former employers, and people I manage with dignity. Explain disagreements through facts, constraints, and decisions rather than insults or speculation about motives.

principles.title: Tell the truth plainly
principles.body: Distinguish what I know, what I infer, and what remains uncertain. Surface problems early, own mistakes, and explain the next step. Make commitments I can defend and communicate changes before they become surprises.

principles.title: Let evidence change my mind
principles.body: Ask simple questions, test assumptions, and look at the results. Take unfamiliar ideas seriously. Explain what changed my view and why. Being useful matters more than being the person who was right first.

principles.title: Learn by building
principles.body: Work directly with the tools and systems I want to understand. Seek feedback from real use. Learn across disciplines and pursue neglected problems when the evidence suggests they matter.

principles.title: Choose useful simplicity
principles.body: Start with a clear solution that meets the actual need. Improve it through measurement and iteration. Invest in reliability, maintainability, and the unglamorous engineering that makes good ideas work in practice.

principles.title: Earn trust through fairness
principles.body: Apply consistent standards, keep promises, and discuss constraints openly. Give others room to question me. Repair misunderstandings and relationships rather than letting resentment become a way of working.

principles.title: Combine ambition with responsibility
principles.body: Be concrete about both the benefit I am pursuing and the harm I need to prevent. Raise concerns with evidence and practical options. Stay hopeful without exaggerating, and take a useful next step.

howIWorkPage.reflection: Did I make the work clearer, the result better, and the team more able to succeed together?

aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.description: About Spencer Imbleau: software engineering, computer graphics, open-source work, and projects.

background.title: A little background
background.body: I like working close to the systems I’m trying to understand: rendering pixels, building tools, and turning experiments into software people can use. My work spans GPU graphics, browser applications, and the infrastructure behind them.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.graphics: I authored and maintain <bevyVello>bevy_vello</bevyVello>, the integration of Vello’s GPU-accelerated vector renderer with Bevy. Alongside other Linebender contributors, I also maintain <velloSvg>vello_svg</velloSvg> and <velato>velato</velato>, working on SVG rendering and Lottie animation.
openSource.tools: I’m a core maintainer of <trunk>Trunk</trunk>, contribute WebAssembly support to <bevy>Bevy</bevy>, and help triage compiler and standard-library issues as a member of the <rust>Rust triage team</rust>.

projects.title: What I build
projects.body: Some of my work becomes a product; some starts with a question about how a system works. These are a few projects I build or help maintain.

contact.title: Let’s talk
contact.body: For engineering, graphics, open source, or a project you’re working on, send me an email or schedule a conversation. You can also find my code and professional profile below.
